summary: This React component adds a discovery link to each blog post's HTML head, pointing crawlers and tools to a plain-Markdown version of the article. It works similarly to how RSS feeds advertise themselves with alternate links, but scoped to individual pages rather than the entire site.

explanations.13: This is a React functional component that returns JSX (the React syntax for HTML-like code). It doesn't take any props as arguments.
explanations.14: useBlogPost() is a Docusaurus hook that gives us metadata about the current blog post we're rendering, like its URL path. We're extracting just the metadata part.
explanations.21: We're building a URL by taking the post's permalink and appending .md to it — so if the article is at /blog/my-post, the Markdown mirror is at /blog/my-post.md.
explanations.22: The translate() function looks up a string in Docusaurus's translation system using that id, falling back to the message if no translation exists. This makes the link's title translatable to other languages.
